title: MATH GAOKAO - 397
description: Authentic-style mathematics problems inspired by China’s Gaokao — build deeper understanding, sharper thinking, and real exam readiness.

questions.concept: Parity of a Sum of Odd Integers
questions.learningObjective: Determine the parity of the sum of two odd integers.
questions.question: Let \(m\) and \(n\) be odd integers. Which expression must be even?
questions.explanation:
An odd integer has the form \(2k+1\). If \(m\) and \(n\) are odd, then
\[
m+n=(2a+1)+(2b+1)=2(a+b+1),
\]
which is divisible by \(2\), so \(m+n\) is even. Adding \(1\) gives an odd number, so \(m+n+1\) is odd.
questions.hint: Write each odd integer in the form \(2k+1\), then combine the terms.

questions.concept: Parity of a Sum of an Even and an Odd Integer
questions.learningObjective: Determine which expression is even when one integer is even and the other is odd.
questions.question: Let \(a\) be an even integer and \(b\) be an odd integer. Which expression must be even?
questions.explanation:
An even integer has the form \(2m\), and an odd integer has the form \(2n+1\). Then
\[
a+b=2m+(2n+1)=2(m+n)+1,
\]
so \(a+b\) is odd. Therefore,
\[
a+b+1=2(m+n+1),
\]
which is even.
questions.hint: Test the parity of \(a+b\) first, then see what adding \(1\) does.

questions.learningObjective: Show that \(n^2+n\) is even for every integer \(n\).
questions.question: For every integer \(n\), the value of \(n^2+n\) is:
questions.explanation:
Factor the expression:
\[
n^2+n=n(n+1).
\]
The integers \(n\) and \(n+1\) are consecutive, so exactly one of them is even. Therefore, their product \(n(n+1)\) is even. Hence \(n^2+n\) is always even.
questions.hint: Factor \(n^2+n\) and consider the parity of two consecutive integers.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the parity of the sum of the first ten positive integers.
questions.question:
The sum
\[
1+2+3+\cdots+10
\]
is:
questions.explanation:
Using the arithmetic series formula,
\[
1+2+3+\cdots+10=\frac{10\cdot 11}{2}=55.
\]
Since \(55\) is not divisible by \(2\), the sum is odd.
questions.hint: Use the formula for the sum of the first \(n\) positive integers.

questions.concept: Parity of a Sum Determined by Counts
questions.learningObjective: Determine the parity of a total sum from the number of odd and even terms.
questions.question: A collection contains \(17\) odd integers and \(26\) even integers. The sum of all these integers must be:
questions.explanation:
The sum of even integers is even, so the \(26\) even integers contribute an even amount. The sum of \(17\) odd integers is odd because the sum of an odd number of odd integers is odd. Therefore, the total sum is
\[
\text{even}+\text{odd}=\text{odd}.
\]
So the total sum must be odd.
questions.hint: Only the number of odd terms affects the parity of the total sum.

questions.concept: Parity of a Difference of Squares
questions.learningObjective: Determine the parity of \(x^2-1\) when \(x\) is odd.
questions.question: If \(x\) is an odd integer, then \(x^2-1\) is:
questions.explanation:
If \(x\) is odd, then \(x^2\) is also odd, because the product of two odd integers is odd. Subtracting \(1\) from an odd integer gives an even integer:
\[
\text{odd}-1=\text{even}.
\]
Thus \(x^2-1\) is even.
questions.hint: First determine the parity of \(x^2\), then subtract \(1\).

questions.concept: Parity of a Quadratic Expression by Factorization
questions.learningObjective: Use factorization to determine the parity of \(n^2+3n+2\).
questions.question:
For every integer \(n\), the value of
\[
n^2+3n+2
\]
is:
questions.explanation:
Factor the quadratic expression:
\[
n^2+3n+2=(n+1)(n+2).
\]
The integers \(n+1\) and \(n+2\) are consecutive, so one of them is even. Therefore, their product is even. Hence \(n^2+3n+2\) is always even.
questions.hint: Factor the quadratic expression and look for consecutive integers.

questions.concept: Determining an Unknown Parity from a Sum
questions.learningObjective: Find the parity of one integer when the parity of its sum with another integer is known.
questions.question: Let \(a,b\) be integers. If \(a+b\) is odd and \(a\) is even, then \(b\) must be:
questions.explanation: An odd sum occurs exactly when the two integers have opposite parity. Since \(a\) is even, the other integer \(b\) must be odd. For example, if \(a=2\), then \(a+b\) is odd only when \(b\) is odd.
questions.hint: Express the given parity information as remainders modulo two, then subtract.

questions.learningObjective: Analyze the parity of \(n^3-n+1\) for every integer \(n\).
questions.question:
For every integer \(n\), the value of
\[
n^3-n+1
\]
is:
questions.explanation:
Factor \(n^3-n\):
\[
n^3-n=n(n^2-1)=n(n-1)(n+1).
\]
This is the product of three consecutive integers. Among three consecutive integers, at least one is even, so \(n^3-n\) is even. Therefore,
\[
n^3-n+1=\text{even}+1=\text{odd}.
\]
Thus \(n^3-n+1\) is always odd.
questions.hint: Factor \(n^3-n\) as a product of consecutive integers.

questions.concept: Parity of a Product Involving Differences
questions.learningObjective: Prove that \(a^3b-ab^3\) is always even for integers \(a\) and \(b\).
questions.question:
For any integers \(a\) and \(b\), the value of
\[
a^3b-ab^3
\]
is:
questions.explanation:
Factor the expression:
\[
a^3b-ab^3=ab(a^2-b^2)=ab(a-b)(a+b).
\]
If at least one of \(a\) or \(b\) is even, then \(ab\) is even, so the whole product is even. If both \(a\) and \(b\) are odd, then \(a-b\) is even, so the product is again even. These are the only possible parity cases, so \(a^3b-ab^3\) is always even.
questions.hint: Factor the expression and consider the cases where \(a\) and \(b\) have the same parity or opposite parity.
